title: SaaS, apps and digital products
tagline: Software, APIs, templates, courses and content sold to customers in India and abroad.
who: Technical founders building a product for global customers
Indie hackers selling templates, plugins or courses

structure.recommended: Private limited company (or a proprietorship until first revenue)
structure.why: Foreign customers, app stores and future investors expect a company; IP sits in the company; ESOPs need shares. If you are solo and pre-revenue, bill on your PAN and incorporate the week the product sells. Think hard before incorporating abroad first — ODI rules and the ‘reverse flip’ trend both point to an Indian parent for Indian founders.
structure.alternatives: LLP for a bootstrapped services-plus-software shop; Delaware C-Corp parent only when a US investor requires it.

breakdown: Cross-border PA onboarding: free; 1–4% per receipt
Audit + ROC + GST filing: ₹35,000–70,000 a year

timeline: Company in 7–15 working days; GST + LUT within a month; first foreign receipt documented with a FIRA the day it lands.
taxes: Exports of services are zero-rated under GST with a LUT if the customer is outside India, payment comes in convertible foreign exchange (or INR via a Vostro account) and you are not an ‘intermediary’. Domestic customers pay 18%.
Selling to Indian consumers through a foreign merchant-of-record (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, app stores) shifts Indian GST collection to them (OIDAR rules); selling direct makes you the GST collector.
Corporate tax 25.17% all-in; DPIIT + Inter-Ministerial Board approval unlocks the 3-of-10-years holiday (old 80-IAC).
Foreign withholding: US customers may ask for Form W-8BEN-E; claim credit under the DTAA in India.
Equalisation levy on online ads was abolished from April 2025; no digital services tax applies to your exports.
selling: Own checkout with Razorpay (INR) + cross-border PA or PayPal (foreign)
Merchant-of-record platforms (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, FastSpring) to outsource global sales tax
App stores (30%/15% commission; Apple/Google collect Indian GST from consumers)
Marketplaces: AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces, Shopify App Store, WordPress.org, Product Hunt launches
sourcing: Cloud and SaaS tools: pay from the company account, claim ITC where GST is charged under reverse charge on imported services (you self-invoice and pay IGST, then take credit)
pitfalls: Receiving export money into a personal account or via a relative — FEMA contravention, and no FIRA means no proof of export for GST.
Forgetting reverse-charge GST on foreign SaaS subscriptions (AWS, Figma billed from abroad) — pay IGST under RCM and claim it back.
Setting up a US LLC ‘for Stripe’ without ODI reporting — even a zero-dollar LLC owned by a resident is reportable; and Stripe India itself is invite-only.
Collecting user data without a DPDP-ready consent notice — full obligations bite from 13 May 2027, and your enterprise customers will ask earlier.
Giving co-founders equity without vesting and without assigning IP to the company.
